Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Gaston
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 02/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 275 as introduced would eliminate: (1) the requirement to publish the Administrative Code in loose-leaf format, which would decrease the postage and printing costs of the Legislative Services Agency (LSA) by approximately $5500, and (2) the subscription charge for the Alabama Administrative Code and the Alabama Administrative Monthly, which would decrease receipts to LSA by an estimated $4,740 annually.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Finance and Taxation Education
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 03/15/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 193 as introduced appropriates from the Education Trust Fund (ETF) Advancement and Technology Fund, for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2021, the amount of $135,096,189 to the public institutions of higher education to be expended as provided by the ETF Rolling Reserve Act.
This bill further appropriates for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2021, from the ETF Advancement and Technology Fund, to the Department of Education to be allocated to the local school systems, the Alabama Institute for Deaf and Blind, the Alabama School of Math and Science, the Alabama School of Fine Arts, the Alabama School of Cyber and Engineering, and the Department of Youth Services School District, the amount of $364,519,895 to be expended as provided by the ETF Rolling Reserve Act. This bill further provides that the funds allocated to the local school systems shall not be expended without prior approval of the State Superintendent of Education and that $2 million of this amount shall be distributed to the Ed Farm Classroom of Tomorrow for technology tools and professional development services to classroom teachers.
In addition, this bill provides that all funds not expended in the current fiscal year shall not revert but be carried forward for the purpose appropriated.
Arthur Orr, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation Education
